field_model.principle: Only explicitly supported values are stored. Absence of evidence is unknown, not false.
field_model.unknown_semantics: A missing canonical field is unknown. False is allowed only when an explicit reliable primary source documents nonexistence or a restriction.
field_model.canonical_path_policy: New curated claims must use active canonical taxonomy paths; deprecated aliases are rejected.

claims.note: Cortex Agents expose a documented agent:run API.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Cortex Agents access control and authentication
evidence.note: Snowflake explicitly states access to Cortex Agents is governed by Snowflake role-based access control.

claims.note: Cortex Agent access uses Snowflake RBAC.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Cortex Agents access control and authentication
evidence.note: Snowflake documents granting the CORTEX_AGENT_USER database role to a custom role for selected users.

claims.note: Custom Snowflake roles can be used to scope Cortex Agent access.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Monitor Cortex Agent requests
evidence.note: Snowflake documents live conversation history, execution traces, planning, tool calls, responses, and feedback for Cortex Agents.

claims.note: Cortex Agent observability includes production conversations and execution telemetry.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Monitor Cortex Agent requests
evidence.note: Snowflake stores OpenTelemetry-style traces and spans for Cortex Agent turns in AI_OBSERVABILITY_EVENTS.

claims.note: Cortex Agent runs produce OpenTelemetry-style trace data.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Monitor Cortex Agent requests
evidence.note: Viewing Cortex Agent logs requires OWNERSHIP or MONITOR on the AGENT plus the CORTEX_USER database role.

claims.note: Monitoring access is explicitly privilege-gated.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Agent identity
evidence.note: Snowflake carries agent identity into QUERY_HISTORY and ACCESS_HISTORY so Cortex Agent activity and accessed objects can be audited.

claims.note: Cortex Agent activity is represented in Snowflake audit/history views.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Federated authentication and SSO
evidence.note: Snowflake documents SAML 2.0 federated authentication for account users; Cortex Agents execute under the querying user's Snowflake role.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Cortex Agents access control and authentication
evidence.note: Cortex Agents uses the querying user's Snowflake identity and default role for permissions.

claims.note: Cortex Agent users can authenticate through Snowflake's SAML SSO controls.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Federated authentication and SSO
evidence.note: Snowflake documents OIDC federated authentication with managed or custom identity providers.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Cortex Agents access control and authentication
evidence.note: Cortex Agents permissions are resolved from the authenticated Snowflake user and default role.

claims.note: Cortex Agent users can authenticate through Snowflake's OIDC federation controls.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – SCIM support
evidence.note: Snowflake supports SCIM 2.0 provisioning of users and groups/roles from identity providers.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Cortex Agents access control and authentication
evidence.note: Cortex Agents access is granted through Snowflake roles and user identities.

claims.note: Users and roles that govern Cortex Agent access can be provisioned through Snowflake SCIM.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Cross-region inference
evidence.note: Snowflake states customer data remains stored only in the account region and cross-region inference can be disabled for strict residency.

claims.note: Cortex AI supports an account-home-region residency posture by disabling cross-region inference.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Supported cloud regions
evidence.note: Snowflake states organizations can choose the region where an account is located and data is geographically stored.

evidence.title: Snowflake Docs – Cross-region inference
evidence.note: Snowflake documents controls to keep Cortex inference in the account home region when required.

claims.note: Organizations choose the Snowflake account region that hosts Cortex Agents and can restrict inference to the home region.
